sentence: A 69-year-old male patient, with a history of partial gastrectomy 30 years ago for peptic gastric ulcer with Billroth II type reconstruction, was admitted with an eight-day history of abdominal pain located in the mesogastrium along with a slight increase in amylase levels. and serum lipase (amylase 550 IU/l, lipase 5976 IU/l).

The abdominal ultrasound showed the distended gallbladder along with a dilation of the intra- and extrahepatic bile ducts and a large cystic formation with thin walls and tubular morphology occupying from the left hypochondrium to the right void, which suggested that it was the dilated afferent loop and filled with liquid.
CT and MRI confirmed these findings.

The upper digestive endoscopy allowed us to visualize the existence of thickened folds in the gastric stump that obstructed the afferent loop, which suggested neoplastic infiltration that was confirmed after the histological study of the endoscopic biopsies.
The patient underwent surgery, with a total gastrectomy and esophagojejunal anastomosis.
